object_L.conclusions: Same rig behaviour as the T (pusher response, coasting) carried over unchanged. The L turns ~2-3x less per unit push relative to how far it translates; COM regressions put the mass near (37, 48) vs the area centroid (37.6, 42.6), i.e. shifted towards the far end of the long leg as the T's was shifted up its stem (weak, per-life fits scatter 26-40 in u). Large initial angle errors (>100 deg) are the hard cases: the program cannot turn the L fast enough within 300 steps.

changes_vs_v15: S10c removed (precision depth back to push units)

what_the_world_showed: S10c (adopted after one real flight) was harmful in aggregate: v15 37.7% vs v14-rules 60.4% (480 imagined episodes); it slowed the end of long episodes (5% vs 56% success at initial |eth| 90-135 deg). One real flight per change could not reveal this.

Failures were dominated by time: success fell from ~0.9 at initial |eth| < 45 deg to 0.0-0.2 above 135 deg; pushing faster (k_depth 0.8, d_max 60) was the one lever that moved every band (60% -> 79%).
Many single-knob changes (COM, g, commitment, translation weight, thresholds) were within noise (+-0.03 at n=240); the world's COM (23.4, 55.6) did not help my program.
0-coverage failures near walls came from a navigation livelock (pusher pinned at the clipped wall line); the orbit-direction fix hurt (81.5%), only a stall watchdog was kept.
distrust: Near-wall starts (block within 40 u of a wall): the world makes the wall a hard stop; success there 0.67-0.71 vs 0.92-0.94 away from walls; I did not tune for wall behaviour and kept only a wall-independent watchdog.
Faster pushes extrapolate: in contact, imagined v17 pusher steps have median 12 / p90 25 / max 51 u per step vs 5.6 / 16 / 37 in my 8 real L lives.
Selection bias: ~45 candidates on the same 240/480 seeds; the submitted program was re-scored on held-out imagined seeds 74000-74479.
